1	# Phase 11.1 — persistent sessions, follow-up turns, resume, and fork
     2	
     3	The session adapters already survive more than one turn. These contracts make that capability
     4	real through the public driver and define the persistence boundary without pretending every vendor
     5	has identical semantics.
     6	
     7	## PS1 — a verified session remains reusable
     8	
     9	After a natural turn is independently verified, the task result is terminal for that turn but the
    10	session handle may remain idle and attached. `send(worker, content, 'turn')` reopens the same pinned
    11	delegation, bumps the coordinator turn epoch, clears only the current result/verdict projection,
    12	and dispatches a native next turn on the same session/process. It is allowed after completed or
    13	failed verification and after a confirmed soft interrupt, but never after kill, crash, timeout,
    14	or unattached replay.
    15	
    16	## PS2 — every follow-up is admitted before state commits
    17	
    18	The coordinator changes idle/terminal state to working only after the adapter returns
    19	`Ack{ok:true}`. Refusal or exception restores the prior result/status and logs no successful turn.
    20	One worker serializes follow-up admission with ordinary send/steer operations. A follow-up uses the
    21	same immutable Brief unless a future explicit refinement command creates a new task contract.
    22	
    23	## PS3 — interrupt-with-follow-up is coordinator-visible
    24	
    25	`interrupt(worker, then)` records `then` in the stop waiter. Once the interrupt Ack and matching
    26	confirmation both arrive, the coordinator reopens the task before the adapter's automatic
    27	follow-up begins. Without `then`, the turn is cancelled and the attached session becomes idle.
    28	Kill always discards pending follow-up. A newer stop supersedes an older follow-up.
    29	
    30	## PS4 — turns are fenced and independently verified
    31	
    32	Coordinator turn generations are authoritative. Each adapter wire epoch is mapped to the current
    33	coordinator epoch at `lifecycle.turn_started`; late terminal/question/approval events from an older
    34	turn are logged as stale and cannot run the trust gate, block the new turn, or overwrite its
    35	result. Every accepted turn receives a fresh capture, verification sandbox, verdict, router
    36	observation, and model attribution.
    37	
    38	## PS5 — native session identity is public and durable
    39	
    40	Wire-observed Claude `sessionId`, Codex `threadId`, and Grok `sessionId` become a typed `sessionRef`
    41	on handle/result/events/replay. The reference includes vendor, kind, id, persistence posture, and
    42	observation source. It is never inferred from a client-generated placeholder.
    43	
    44	## PS6 — resume and fork are explicit spawn policies
    45	
    46	`spawn(..., {session:{mode,id,lastTurnId?}})` supports `new`, `resume`, and `fork` when the card
    47	declares them. Claude maps resume/fork to `--resume ID [--fork-session]`; Codex maps to
    48	`thread/resume`/`thread/fork`; Grok maps resume to `session/load`. Grok's documented
    49	`x.ai/session/fork` and rewind surface remain carded `planned` until their exact installed wire
    50	schemas are pinned and fixture-tested; Baton must not advertise them as native merely because the
    51	vendor has them. Unsupported combinations fail typed before allocation. Fork creates a new
    52	task/session identity and never aliases the parent worker's mutable state.
    53	
    54	## PS7 — restart recovery is honest before it is automatic
    55	
    56	Replay restores session references but does not claim control until an adapter proves reattachment.
    57	`recover(worker, {timeoutMs?,context?})` attempts bounded native resume/rejoin when explicitly
    58	requested, records success/failure, and only then changes `orphaned` to working. The fresh
    59	handshake must report exactly the persisted native session identity; mismatch, refusal, exception,
    60	or timeout kills the untrusted transport and leaves the handle orphaned. PID identity requires a
    61	birth token or native session handshake; a replayed numeric PID alone is never signalled because
    62	of PID reuse.
    63	
    64	## PS8 — worktree and fork coherence
    65	
    66	Resume requires a durable context containing at least the exact worktree and its owner task, then
    67	validates repository/base/branch/worktree ownership before dispatch. Fork receives a new worktree
    68	and explicit parent-session/refinement edge. Vendor history resume never
    69	silently restores file changes into the main checkout; rewinds/forks distinguish conversational
    70	history from filesystem state and are independently verified after the next turn.
    71	
    72	## Safety gate
    73	
    74	PS1-PS5 require fake-backed driver tests for Claude, Codex, and Grok. PS6-PS8 require protocol
    75	fixture coverage before provider probes. Live proof must show a verified first turn, a public
    76	follow-up on the same native session and PID, a second independent verification, then confirmed
    77	kill/reap. Native resume/fork probes follow only after persisted references and worktree-coherence
    78	checks are green.

1	# 26 — Full-system goal: no planned capability disappears
     2	
     3	This is the plan of record after the 2026-07-11 completeness audit. It supersedes any reading of
     4	docs 22–25 that treats “phase 10 complete” as completion of Baton’s larger design. Phase 10 proved
     5	a useful first-turn control spine. The active goal is the complete fleet system described across
     6	`SYSTEM.md`, `docs/`, `spec/`, and `reviews/`.
     7	
     8	“Later”, “fenced”, and “research bet” are sequencing/status labels, not deletion mechanisms. Every
     9	item below remains visible until it is either shipped with evidence or explicitly retired by a
    10	recorded, evidence-backed decision. A feature cannot vanish from the goal through a summary.
    11	
    12	## Scope correction
    13	
    14	The shared knowledge design takes architectural inspiration from `project-manager`, but Baton has
    15	**no homelab integration or runtime dependency** in this goal. It owns a deployment-neutral typed
    16	causal substrate and may expose ordinary import/export interfaces later. This avoids coupling the
    17	product to one machine or knowledge service.
    18	
    19	## Definition of complete
    20	
    21	Baton is complete when one orchestrator can choose harness **and model**, direct persistent
    22	multi-vendor workers through a durable northbound surface, observe and govern them safely, accept
    23	and integrate only independently established work, share operational/coordinative/epistemic
    24	knowledge, and give workers the complete capability and representation planes below. Every claim
    25	must be reachable through the public assembly, test-locked, adversarially reviewed, and live-proven
    26	where a real harness or operating-system boundary is involved.
    27	
    28	The implementation loop for every increment is:
    29	
    30	1. verify current reality;
    31	2. write numbered contracts;
    32	3. capture a red test or measured failing probe;
    33	4. implement the smallest complete vertical;
    34	5. run narrow and full validation;
    35	6. adversarially review seams, not only modules;
    36	7. live-prove the real boundary; and
    37	8. update this catalog and the evidence ledger.
    38	
    39	Recursive dogfooding resumes only after the lifecycle, provenance, and credential gates relevant
    40	to the recursive run are green.
    41	
    42	## Complete capability catalog
    43	
    44	### A. Fleet control and reliability
    45	
    46	- Eight public commands: spawn, send, wait, respond, interrupt, result, list, kill.
    47	- Ordered delivery, human-over-policy fencing, single-consumer interactions, two-phase stop,
    48	  terminal monotonicity, bounded setup/turn/stop operations, and process/worktree reap.
    49	- Persistent multi-turn workers; interrupt-follow-up; resume, fork, rejoin, checkpoint, rewind, and
    50	  crash recovery without fabricating uniform semantics across vendors.
    51	- Restart-safe task/worker identity, pending interactions, fences, adapter/session references,
    52	  worktree ownership, story, budgets, and routing state.
    53	- Dependency DAG, refinement links, idempotent claims, artifact registry, path leases, and
    54	  deterministic ready-work selection.
    55	
    56	### B. Harness and model selection
    57	
    58	Harness/CLI and model are independent axes. The orchestrator can:
    59	
    60	- name an exact harness and exact model;
    61	- select a model while leaving harness routing automatic;
    62	- constrain allowed/denied models or families and express ordered preferences;
    63	- select reasoning/service tier where the harness exposes it;
    64	- inspect available/default/current model information and the provenance/freshness of that card;
    65	- see requested, resolved, observed, and rerouted model identities in handles, events, results,
    66	  verification, routing statistics, replay, scorecards, and commit attribution; and
    67	- fail visibly when a model cannot be honored—never silently fall back to a harness default.
    68	
    69	Selection must map to real controls: Claude/GLM `--model`, Codex thread/turn model overrides, Grok
    70	`--model`/ACP model state, and future adapters’ native mechanism.
    71	
    72	### C. Southbound harness depth
    73	
    74	- Claude: native session steering/interrupt, approvals/questions, hooks, context/usage
    75	  introspection, compaction events, constraint reinjection, model/permission reconfiguration,
    76	  resume/fork/rewind, config-home isolation, and live capability discovery.
    77	- Codex: app-server sessions, steer/interrupt, approvals/questions, thread inject/resume/fork,
    78	  goal pinning, structured outputs, review, compaction, usage/rate limits, broker/daemon topology,
    79	  model/service/reasoning selection, sandbox policy, and schema-driven feature detection.
    80	- Grok: ACP core plus model selection/state, session load/fork/rewind, auth, extensions, usage,
    81	  multi-client attach, home/MCP isolation, and explicit handling of unsupported ask-user behavior.
    82	- GLM: Claude-harness session parity, exact model mapping, non-refuser capability metadata,
    83	  concurrency/quota inputs, scoped credentials, and live proof when credentials are available.
    84	- Honest one-shot tier and future ACP adapters remain separately carded; no reduced tier may pose
    85	  as the session product.
    86	
    87	### D. Safety and governance
    88	
    89	- Real OS sandbox profiles, worktree confinement, network policy, scoped environment/credentials,
    90	  isolated harness homes, and approval-gated outside-world side effects.
    91	- Dry-run/approve-all/sample/autonomous trust ramp with emergency stop always available.
    92	- Wall, token, USD, rate-limit, account-seat, and quota-window budgets folded into authoritative
    93	  state with thresholds, hard stops, and degradation policies.
    94	- Deterministic watchdog actions for mechanical stall/loop/scope/churn cases; semantic failure
    95	  classifiers remain explicitly untrusted model judgments.
    96	- Correct provenance: hub facts, worker prose, external evidence, and derived claims never share a
    97	  trust label. Read edges support contamination/contradiction analysis.
    98	
    99	### E. Trust, review, and integration
   100	
   101	- Immutable validated delegation contract and exact definition of done.
   102	- Fresh-result verification plus base red→green, coverage-of-change, mutation strength,
   103	  impact-selected tests, property/fuzz/BMC/SMT/proof rungs, and reproducible counterexamples.
   104	- Independent oracle construction and cross-vendor semantic-diff review for risk-selected work.
   105	- Structured postmortems and failure attribution linked to source events.
   106	- Verified branch integration, textual then structured/semantic merge, conflict handling, effect
   107	  tripwire, review artifact, and explicit approval before push/deploy/other irreversible actions.
   108	
   109	### F. Routing, evaluation, and learning
   110	
   111	- Routing buckets keyed by harness, exact model, model family, task class, capability, policy, and
   112	  version; only verified outcomes learn; idempotent replay preserves them.
   113	- New-model exploration, decay, refusal feedback/reroute, operator pin/exclude/prefer controls,
   114	  quota awareness, and outcome/calibration telemetry.
   115	- Reproducible M0 control latency, M1 orchestration arms, and E2 cross-vendor decorrelation
   116	  evaluations, including null/negative outcomes and human-audit cost.
   117	
   118	### G. Three memory tempos plus Scratch
   119	
   120	- **Operational:** append-only event ledger, resumable cursors, replay, artifacts, and telemetry.
   121	- **Coordinative:** transactional task DAG, artifact manifest, claims/leases, refinements, and
   122	  ready-work queries.
   123	- **Epistemic:** durable typed causal knowledge with bounded recall.
   124	- **Scratch:** TTL/CAS/take/notify blackboard and memoized Bench for fleet-live facts and leases.
   125	
   126	The epistemic layer borrows the strong ideas—not the deployment—from `project-manager`:
   127	
   128	- typed nodes: Run, Task, Artifact, Experiment, Finding, Decision, Hypothesis, Principle,
   129	  Constraint, Source/Literature, RouteStat, Skill, Counterexample, and Representation;
   130	- typed directional edges: Supports, Contradicts, Supersedes, Informed, ProducedBy, Contains,
   131	  DependsOn, Refines, ReadBy, VerifiedBy, and DerivedFrom;
   132	- every consequential decision has evidence edges to earlier immutable ledger events;
   133	- temporal coherence forbids an edge to evidence that did not yet exist;
   134	- bitemporal validity preserves what was believed then versus what is valid now;
   135	- selective promotion avoids turning every event into knowledge;
   136	- contradiction-gated, provenance-framed, token-bounded pull recall—never automatic shared-brain
   137	  injection; and
   138	- run scorecards expose graph and fleet health with metric breakdowns rather than one green bit.
   139	
   140	### H. Capability plane
   141	
   142	Every capability uses one ACI envelope, capability cards, cost/provenance, resumable long work,
   143	cancellation, and hub re-verification.
   144	
   145	1. **Atlas:** shared lexical search, AST/CST structural search/rewrite, symbol graph and SCIP/LSP
   146	   navigation, optional semantic retrieval, base-plus-worktree overlays, staleness, and `code_seed`.
   147	2. **Vantage:** DAP observation plans, causal debugging results, record/replay assets, exclusive
   148	   debuggee leases, and reproducible postmortems.
   149	3. **Evidence Ladder:** tests through proof with honest language/tool ceilings, mutation scores,
   150	   trusted kernels, full dependency-closure hashes, and no “proven” claim over worker-weakened
   151	   specifications.
   152	4. **Scratch:** operational blackboard/coordination REPL and memoized experiment Bench.
   153	5. **Skill Forge and computer use:** verify, promote, version, revoke, and share portable skills;
   154	   distill flaky GUI trajectories into deterministic automation where possible.
   155	6. **Cartographer and Quartermaster:** shared repository orientation/call graphs plus gated
   156	   dependency/reuse/security evidence.
   157	7. **Cairn:** run scorecards, causal findings/decisions, route statistics, promotion, recall,
   158	   contradiction/supersession, and exportable body of knowledge.
   159	
   160	### I. Representation and computation ladder
   161	
   162	Representation is negotiated by task phase and cost, not reduced to raw text:
   163	
   164	- R0 text/tokens;
   165	- R1 CST/AST via tree-sitter/ast-grep/difftastic/GumTree-class edit scripts;
   166	- R2 symbol/call/dependency graphs via LSP, SCIP, stack graphs, or equivalent;
   167	- R3 code property graph: AST + CFG + PDG/dataflow/taint, including CPG deltas;
   168	- R4 compiler/intermediate representations for optimization and translation validation;
   169	- R5 behavioral fingerprints from differential/property/fuzz execution and effect signatures;
   170	- R6 structured and semantic diff/merge over syntax, symbols, control/data-flow, and behavior;
   171	- R7 e-graph/equality-saturation experiments where the domain is tractable; and
   172	- representation choreography: orient with a coarse graph, focus with local AST/CPG, finish with
   173	  a semantic delta and attestation overlay, retracting views no longer useful.
   174	
   175	The first shipped vertical is AST/structural delta for review. CPG, semantic merge, behavioral
   176	fingerprints, IR, and e-graphs remain in the goal with explicit prototype/evaluation gates; a
   177	negative result retires a rung through a recorded Decision, never through omission.
   178	
   179	### J. Context, operator, northbound, and runtime
   180	
   181	- Vendor-shaped briefs, addressed context, orientation references, constraint/DoD reinjection on
   182	  compaction, context usage governance, and retractable views.
   183	- MCP northbound fleet tools and tasks, a long-lived daemon, resumable waits/subscriptions, and an
   184	  operator text/TUI seat with narrative, provenance, takeover, approvals, budgets, and emergency
   185	  control.
   186	- An **authenticated web northbound** for the human user ↔ orchestrator direction. HTTPS command
   187	  requests and a resumable WebSocket/event stream expose the same coordinator authority—not a
   188	  parallel state machine—including spawn/harness/model selection, steer/nudge/turn, approval and
   189	  question response, interrupt/kill, goals/tasks, narrative, budgets, and emergency control.
   190	  Authentication binds a stable user/session identity; authorization scopes commands and repo/run
   191	  access; every command carries an idempotency key, fence expectation, origin, and audit actor.
   192	  TLS, secure session/token storage, expiry/revocation, origin and CSRF checks, replay protection,
   193	  rate limits, reconnect cursors, backpressure, and disconnect semantics are contract-tested.
   194	  Browser loss never cancels work implicitly, and the web tier cannot bypass approval, sandbox,
   195	  budget, or trust gates. A richer visual UI is optional; the secure control connection is not.
   196	  Numbered contracts and its adversarial gate live in
   197	  `spec/phase12/authenticated-web-northbound.md` (WN1–WN10).
   198	- Observability exports use OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions.
   199	- One-machine production first, with a reliable Go or Elixir/OTP core after the executable-spec
   200	  contracts stabilize. Remote/multi-machine execution remains catalogued but is not allowed to
   201	  distort the local correctness boundary.
   202	
   203	## Current pursuit order
   204	
   205	1. Repair P0 control integrity: immutable briefs, truthful responses, crash-safe idempotent kill,
   206	   provenance, story identity, replay identity, and complete cleanup.
   207	2. Ship harness-independent exact model selection and attribution.
   208	3. Make persistent sessions genuinely usable through the driver; add resume/fork/rejoin.
   209	4. Ship OS/credential isolation and budget/watchdog governance.
   210	5. Complete hardened acceptance and structured integration.
   211	6. Ship the task/artifact/Scratch substrate and deployment-neutral causal knowledge core.
   212	7. Ship Atlas + AST structural delta + repo map + scorecard as the first capability vertical.
   213	8. Expand the representation and capability ladders in measured increments.
   214	9. Add MCP plus authenticated HTTPS/WebSocket user↔orchestrator control, operator surfaces,
   215	   production runtime, and the registered evaluations.
   216	
   217	No later step is permission to erase it from the goal.

1	# Phase 11.3 — acceptance ladder and integration lifecycle
     2	
     3	## AC1 — red then green is measured at pinned commits
     4	
     5	When required, Baton runs the exact pinned verification command in both a fresh base-SHA sandbox
     6	and a distinct fresh result-SHA sandbox. Acceptance requires base failure and result success. Both
     7	sandboxes are always reaped, including setup/referee failure paths.
     8	
     9	## AC2 — coverage is computed from the actual delta
    10	
    11	When required, Baton computes changed line numbers between the pinned base and captured result,
    12	runs the brief's coverage command in the result sandbox, and accepts only when every changed line
    13	is reported executed. Missing/malformed coverage is unknown and cannot satisfy a required gate.
    14	
    15	## AC3 — mutation strength is an explicit rung
    16	
    17	An optional pinned mutation command runs only after the primary result check passes and returns
    18	JSON `{killed,total,survived[]}`. The verdict records strength and survivors. Required mutation
    19	acceptance demands a nonzero mutant population and no survivor; malformed/missing evidence is
    20	unknown, never success.
    21	
    22	## AC4 — independent oracle and review provenance
    23	
    24	Oracle tests and risk-selected reviews are separate tasks with a different eligible vendor/model
    25	family from the implementer. Their briefs receive the immutable spec and captured diff/artifact
    26	references, not the implementer's prose answer. Oracle/review results pass their own trust gates
    27	and become explicit acceptance inputs; same-family fallback is visible and cannot satisfy a
    28	required independent gate.
    29	
    30	## AC5 — verified integration is explicit and local-first
    31	
    32	`integrate(worker)` is allowed only for an accepted captured SHA. Baton first stops/reaps the
    33	attached worker, then applies an explicit strategy. The first shipped strategy is `ff-only`: main
    34	must be clean and still descend directly from the task base. Success records before/result/after
    35	SHAs and marks the task integrated. Before branch cleanup Baton pins the captured SHA under
    36	`refs/baton/results/<sha>`; success releases the pin because main retains it, while refusal keeps
    37	the pin as durable evidence. Non-fast-forward state refuses without rewriting history.
    38	
    39	## AC6 — irreversible publication requires a separate approval
    40	
    41	Push/deploy is not implied by verification or local integration. A publication request is a
    42	single-consumer approval containing remote/ref/SHA; only an explicit allow response may invoke the
    43	side effect. Deny, timeout, replay, stale fence, or missing approval performs no push. Secret
    44	remote credentials never enter the event payload. The remote is a configured credential-free name,
    45	the branch is a full `refs/heads/*` ref, and the SHA must equal the locally integrated result.
    46	
    47	## Safety gate
    48	
    49	Temp-repo tests prove base/result freshness, coverage, mutation parsing, sandbox cleanup,
    50	integration success/refusal, and no-push-without-approval before any provider or remote probe.

1	# Phase 11.4 — durable coordination and knowledge substrate
     2	
     3	This specification implements goal catalog A/G and the Scratch/Cairn portions of H without a
     4	homelab or `project-manager` runtime dependency. `project-manager` is prior-art inspiration for
     5	typed causal structure and audits only. Baton owns a deployment-neutral, single-host-first event
     6	store and deterministic projections.
     7	
     8	The first implementation vertical is deliberately one substrate, not four unrelated databases:
     9	task, artifact, Scratch, and knowledge mutations are typed coordination events. The append-only
    10	event file is truth; every query result is a replayable projection.
    11	
    12	## CK1 — one durable coordination stream
    13	
    14	`CoordinationStore(root)` owns an append-only `events.jsonl` with gap-free global `seq`, hub-stamped
    15	ISO time, schema version, `kind`, authenticated/audited `actor`, idempotency key, and JSON payload.
    16	Only the hub writes. An append is durable before its projection mutates. Duplicate idempotency keys
    17	return the original event without a second mutation. Torn/malformed tails fail startup visibly;
    18	they are never silently reset or skipped. Replay produces byte-equivalent public projections.
    19	
    20	The store path is explicitly supplied by the assembly and never derived from a worker cwd. It has
    21	no network, PM, or homelab dependency.
    22	
    23	### CK1a — relation to per-worker operational logs
    24	
    25	Existing `<worker>.jsonl` streams remain lossless high-volume operational telemetry with local
    26	per-worker sequence numbers. They are not a second task/KG truth. Every state-changing driver path
    27	first appends its typed coordination mutation; only then may the in-memory task/artifact/Scratch/KG
    28	projection change. Operational evidence is referenced as `{worker, seq, digest}` and becomes
    29	cross-worker comparable only through an `evidence.mapped` coordination event whose global sequence
    30	is the observation order. Knowledge temporal checks use the global coordination sequence, never a
    31	bare per-worker sequence.
    32	
    33	The two files cannot be transactionally committed together. Reconciliation therefore scans
    34	operational evidence references at startup: an operational event with no coordination mutation is
    35	telemetry only and cannot affect task/KG truth; a coordination event pointing to missing or
    36	digest-mismatched operational evidence fails integrity validation. Coordination append failure is
    37	fatal to the requested state mutation and leaves its projection unchanged. It may not use the
    38	legacy warning-and-drop behavior of the telemetry sink.
    39	
    40	Construction validates the complete coordination stream immediately: JSON parse, schema version,
    41	gap-free sequence, unique idempotency key, and final newline. A truncated/torn tail is an
    42	actionable startup error and is never auto-truncated. Schema migration is explicit versioned event
    43	translation into a new store, not in-place reinterpretation.
    44	
    45	## CK2 — typed durable task DAG and claims
    46	
    47	A task record contains:
    48	
    49	```text
    50	id, brief, status, deps[], assignee, version, refines, taskType,
    51	createdEvent, claimedEvent, terminalEvent, artifactIds[]
    52	```
    53	
    54	Status is `pending | working | input_required | completed | failed | cancelled`. Terminal states
    55	are immutable. Allowed nonterminal transitions are explicit. Creation rejects missing deps and
    56	cycles. A task is ready iff it is pending, unassigned, and every dependency is completed.
    57	`claimTask(id, worker, expectedVersion, key)` is compare-and-swap: exactly one concurrent caller
    58	wins; stale, blocked, already-assigned, and terminal claims are typed refusals and do not append.
    59	Refinement creates a new task with `refines`; it never reopens a terminal task.
    60	
    61	Coordinator `spawn()` durably creates the task before returning a handle, including when the task
    62	will remain queued. It may preallocate a public pending worker handle as a local reservation, but
    63	the durable task `assignee` remains null until dispatch wins `claimTask`; reservation is not claim.
    64	Dispatch durably claims it. Input waits, recovery, cancellation, verification
    65	accept/reject, and integration/publication outcomes are reflected by typed events. Restart rebuilds
    66	queued tasks, dependency readiness, assignments, terminal state, and automatic identifiers before
    67	dispatching anything.
    68	
    69	Every adapter- or outside-world-reaching action has a durable intent before the effect: stop,
    70	persistent follow-up, recovery attach, review-task creation, local integration, publication
    71	request, and publication authorization. If intent append fails, no adapter, worktree/Git merge, or
    72	publisher is called. If an adapter has already confirmed stop/attach/turn advancement when a later
    73	terminal/refinement append fails, the coordinator is poisoned, resolves any public waiter with a
    74	typed coordination-unavailable result, kills or quarantines the ambiguous transport, and restart
    75	closes the still-nonterminal durable task. Asynchronous adapter callbacks may not turn an already
    76	recorded fatal coordination fault into an uncaught process exception.
    77	
    78	`task.created` persists `brief`, `deps`, `refines`, `taskType`, requested vendor/model/session
    79	policy, and the reserved public handle ID. `task.claimed` persists assignee, resolved vendor/model,
    80	and expected/new versions. Refusal codes are `stale_version | already_assigned |
    81	deps_unsatisfied | terminal | cycle`; refusals append no event. Recovery terminalization refines or
    82	terminates the durable record and may never reopen a terminal predecessor.
    83	
    84	## CK3 — immutable artifact manifest
    85	
    86	Artifacts are manifests, never copied bytes:
    87	
    88	```text
    89	id, taskId, kind, refs, mediaType, digest, size?, provenance[], createdEvent
    90	```
    91	
    92	Kinds include `commit | diff | verification | coverage | mutation | review | report |
    93	counterexample | representation | skill | bench-result`. `refs` are Git SHAs/refs or explicit
    94	content-addressed paths owned by Baton. Registration validates the task, snapshots caller-owned
    95	data, and is idempotent by manifest identity. `artifact.registered` names the immutable manifest;
    96	`artifact.superseded` links a correction without mutation. Failed/cancelled tasks may register
    97	counterexamples, logs, and reports, but an artifact marked `accepted` must cite the accepting
    98	verification/review event. Accepted capture, verdict, independent review, integration, and
    99	publication payloads carry manifest IDs through the public driver rather than leaving provenance
   100	split across `capturedSha` and worker prose.
   101	
   102	## CK4 — Scratch is an event-derived operational projection
   103	
   104	Scratch supports the smallest worker-useful primitives:
   105	
   106	- append-only facts with namespace/key, immutable `envRef:{repoId,treeSha}`, `observed | derived`
   107	  grounding, evidence refs,
   108	  and optional explicit expiry event;
   109	- advisory claims with resource glob, owner worker/task, intent, `envRef`, supervisor fence,
   110	  version, and lease deadline;
   111	- point checks that return clear/held plus a mandatory cross-environment warning when the fact or
   112	  claim was observed on another tree; and
   113	- explicit `scratch.claim_expired` / `scratch.fact_expired` events.
   114	
   115	There is no reader-clock expiry, heartbeat verb, free-text fleet chat, mutable world-state blob, or
   116	general CAS document in the first vertical. Claim expiry is a hub-emitted event slaved to worker
   117	lease/terminal state, so replay at different wall times is identical. Path-resource conflicts use
   118	conservative glob intersection; uncertain overlap conflicts rather than false-negatives. Exclusive
   119	OS resources remain the sandbox/allocator's job, not an advisory Scratch claim.
   120	
   121	Worker-facing participation is eventually ambient through mediated tool results; until that tool
   122	path ships, the public store exposes deterministic point checks rather than a polling/watch loop.
   123	Live worktree paths are invalid environment references; callers snapshot `git write-tree` (or an
   124	equivalent content digest) before posting. A different `treeSha` always produces the exact warning
   125	frame `observed on <treeSha> — not your tree`.
   126	
   127	Normative path-claim overlap is conservative: normalize repository-relative POSIX paths; exact
   128	paths overlap on equality; a glob overlaps an exact path if the path matches; two globs overlap if
   129	either literal prefix before its first wildcard is a prefix of the other or an implementation can
   130	exhibit a matching witness. If disjointness cannot be proven, they conflict. This may false-positive
   131	but may not false-negative a known overlap.
   132	
   133	## CK5 — self-contained typed bitemporal causal knowledge graph
   134	
   135	The graph is a materialized view over coordination events. It supports typed nodes:
   136	
   137	```text
   138	Run, Task, Artifact, Phase, Experiment, Finding, Decision, Hypothesis, Principle,
   139	Constraint, Literature, Research, RouteStat, Skill, Counterexample, Representation,
   140	ScratchFact
   141	```
   142	
   143	and typed directional edges:
   144	
   145	```text
   146	Supports, Contradicts, Supersedes, Informed, ProducedBy, Contains, DependsOn,
   147	Refines, ReadBy, VerifiedBy, DerivedFrom, Affects, Cites, ObservedIn
   148	```
   149	
   150	Every node and edge stores observation time (coordination seq/time), event time (referenced source
   151	seq/time), and valid time (`validFrom`, nullable `validTo`). Invalidated beliefs are never deleted.
   152	`Supersedes` and contradiction resolution append invalidation events with compare-and-swap on the
   153	current validity version.
   154	
   155	A Decision is rejected unless it has at least one `Informed` evidence reference. A verified
   156	Finding is rejected unless it has `ProducedBy`/`VerifiedBy` evidence. Temporal coherence rejects
   157	evidence whose source sequence/time is later than the node or edge event time. Worker/recalled text
   158	is always marked untrusted prose; grounding is hub-derived (`verified | observed | derived |
   159	asserted`) and never taken from a model confidence float.
   160	
   161	`queryKnowledge({asOf, observedAt, types, grounding})` applies both temporal dimensions.
   162	`traceKnowledge(id)` returns causal paths to immutable events/artifacts. Recall is pull-only,
   163	token-bounded at the caller, contradiction-aware, provenance-framed, and logged with `ReadBy`;
   164	nothing is automatically injected into a worker context.
   165	
   166	The durable read record is `knowledge.read{readerActor, readerWorker, runId, taskId, nodeIds[],
   167	query, asOf, observedAt, validityVersions}`. Its append must succeed before recalled content is
   168	returned. The graph projection creates `ReadBy` edges from every returned node to the reader task/
   169	run. An unlogged read is a failed operation, never a degraded success.
   170	
   171	## CK6 — selective promotion and health
   172	
   173	Promotion is deterministic candidate generation, not an LLM in the control path:
   174	
   175	- accepted terminal task + verification/artifact → `knowledge.promoted{kind:'Finding'}`;
   176	- consequential human/orchestrator spawn, reroute, accept, integrate, publish, abort → Decision;
   177	- run boundary → Run scorecard;
   178	- repeated verified outcome → RouteStat/Playbook candidate;
   179	- cited observed Scratch fact → `knowledge.promotion_candidate{kind:'Finding'}`;
   180	- derived/formal Scratch fact remains quarantined until an independent oracle links it.
   181	
   182	The first vertical implements explicit node/edge writes plus named task/artifact auto-promotion
   183	hooks. Failed/unaccepted tasks never auto-promote a positive Finding; they may promote a
   184	Counterexample or failure Finding with explicit grounding.
   185	Later scorecard/recall promotion uses the same schema. `auditKnowledge()` reports causal
   186	completeness, temporal coherence, orphan nodes, contradiction resolution, invalid references,
   187	recall utility, and read-contamination blast radius separately—never one unexplained green bit.
   188	
   189	## CK7 — contamination and read provenance
   190	
   191	Every knowledge or Scratch read that crosses into an orchestrator/worker context records reader,
   192	run/task, returned IDs, query/as-of boundary, and source validity versions through
   193	`knowledge.read`. If a node is later invalidated,
   194	`knowledge.contamination_record{nodeId, invalidationEvent, affectedReadEvents[]}` is appended and
   195	`affectedReaders(id)` projects every downstream task/run that consumed it, including current task
   196	status. A
   197	cross-tree Scratch read is labeled “observed on X — not your tree.” This is required before shared
   198	knowledge can influence routing or acceptance.
   199	
   200	## CK8 — authority and public assembly
   201	
   202	The store is mandatory in `createDriver()` and returned as `{coordinator, story, router, log,
   203	coordination}`. The coordinator receives it in its constructor and invokes one non-optional
   204	state-changing integration point for spawn/create, dispatch/claim, input wait/resume, terminal,
   205	capture/verification, review, integration, and publication. A driver state mutation with no
   206	coordination event is a contract failure, not an optional sink failure. Direct mutation methods
   207	require an actor and
   208	idempotency key; future MCP/web surfaces map authenticated identity into that same actor field and
   209	do not bypass coordinator fences or approvals. Knowledge export/import is ordinary data I/O behind
   210	future approval gates, not a special PM/homelab integration.
   211	
   212	## CK9 — zero-quota safety gate
   213	
   214	Temp-directory and temp-Git tests must prove before provider dogfooding:
   215	
   216	1. duplicate append keys and duplicate task creates are idempotent;
   217	2. queued/unassigned tasks and dependency readiness survive restart;
   218	3. claim CAS has exactly one winner and terminal states cannot reopen;
   219	4. cycles, stale versions, invalid transitions, and missing deps refuse without events;
   220	5. artifact manifests are immutable and linked to accepted tasks;
   221	6. Scratch conflicts, explicit lease expiry, replay determinism, and cross-tree warnings;
   222	7. causal/temporal graph rejections, bitemporal as-of query, contradiction/supersession history,
   223	   and affected-reader tracing;
   224	8. public-driver task creation, terminal verdict, captured commit, review, and integration appear
   225	   in the durable substrate; and
   226	9. a full restart has identical task/artifact/Scratch/KG projections before any new dispatch.
   227	10. an unsatisfied-dependency task crashes before dispatch and replays pending, unassigned, with
   228	    its exact `deps[]`, brief, requested vendor/model/session, and reserved handle identity;
   229	11. a multi-task DAG replays with the same ready set and cannot dispatch a dependent early;
   230	12. a truncated tail, sequence gap, duplicate key, missing operational evidence, and injected
   231	    append failure all fail visibly without projection mutation;
   232	13. every public spawn/claim/input/terminal/capture/review/integration/publication state change has
   233	    a coordination event, and the test fails if coordinator state is nonempty while the substrate
   234	    stream is empty;
   235	14. operational evidence mapping gives two worker-local events a comparable global observation
   236	    order without treating their local sequences as globally ordered; and
   237	15. after a logged knowledge read, invalidating the node yields a nonempty contamination record
   238	    and `affectedReaders()` result; a forced read-log append failure returns no recalled content.
   239	16. injected append failures cover create, claim, input wait/resume, stop intent, cancel terminal,
   240	    persistent follow-up/recovery refinement, review creation, terminal artifact batch,
   241	    integration intent, publication authorization, and knowledge/Scratch reads. Pre-effect
   242	    failures call no adapter/Git/publisher; post-effect failures are bounded, poison authority,
   243	    preserve the earlier intent, and replay to a non-success terminal state.
   244	
   245	After CK9 is green and committed, Baton may recursively run a real provider review against this
   246	spec and implementation. The recursive task must use isolated runtime credentials/budgets, exact
   247	model selection, a pinned verification command, independent trust-gate verification, and confirmed
   248	kill/process/worktree/branch cleanup.
   249	
   250	## Explicitly later, never deleted
   251	
   252	- durable pending question/approval reconstruction and automatic live-session rejoin;
   253	- a SQLite/other query index (projection only), multi-process writer locking, and multi-machine
   254	  replication;
   255	- ambient Scratch injection in tool mediation, Bench action-cache execution, notify subscriptions,
   256	  and task promotion from contention;
   257	- automatic scorecards, bounded lexical/graph recall ranking, RouteStat feedback, Playbook/Skill
   258	  promotion, and import/export tooling;
   259	- authenticated MCP/HTTPS/WebSocket access (uses this substrate but ships in its own phase); and
   260	- graph-backed Atlas/CPG/representation nodes (schema is reserved here; producers ship later).

I’m checking replay semantics now, especially whether an effect that has already happened but lost its completion append is only bounded in-process or is also closed correctly after restart. That distinction matters because CK9 requires restart closure, not just an immediate poison path.
